messages.author: f96bd3fc938b6150
messages.subject: Confused about packrat/src
parts:
I'm still trying to get my head around how Packrat works. I initially added packrat/src to my .gitignore because I didn't want the tarball sources in the repo. That caused problems because the system got hung up when trying to install some packages (`mnormt`, for instance). So I thought thought that maybe if I added packrat/src to the repo, then I could get around the problem. However, the system is still freezing up when installing the package (and messages in the console are telling me that the binaries for other packages are being downloaded. I checked the packrat.opts and `vcs.ignore.src` is set to FALSE.  Am I missing something obvious? 

Thanks in advance,
Joe

I sort see why this happened (gfortran), and I suppose PackRat is not to blame. (If I understand correctly, I have to install fortran-4.8 on the machine where it isn't working?). The problem is that I really don't know what would be installed on other people's machines (for someone else, the installation stalled on a different package, and I imagine this package is a dependency, since I didn't call it myself). Is there any way around the issue?

messages.author: ab0d2be2ea8dabe8
messages.subject: Re: Confused about packrat/src
parts:
Hi Joe,

Roughly speaking, 'snapshot()' is used to 'save' the state of your
library -- packrat looks at the active library paths, and downloads
package sources for all packages available. 'restore()' will 'load'
that state, attempting to reinstall all packages from the last
snapshot. This is done from CRAN binaries if available, and from
sources if not.

The error you saw for mnormt:

gfortran-4.8 -fPIC -g -O2 -c biv-nt.f -o biv-nt.o
make: gfortran-4.8: No such file or directory

implies that packrat was attempting to install the package from
source. In this case, it requires gfortran to be available on the
system, to compile some bundled FORTRAN files in the package. Guessing
that you are on OS X, you likely need to install Xcode to get access
to clang (for compilation of C / C++ source code in packages), as well
as the gfortran-4.8 package distributed by Simon Urbanek here:

http://r.research.att.com/libs/gfortran-4.8.2-darwin13.tar.bz2

So, my best guess is that you need to make sure compilers / Xcode are
available and installed on your system.

Thanks,
Kevin
